title: Audit: quadratic rounding accumulation and linear-error Neumann evaluation (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Adversarial audit / conditional precision refinement; no new κ.** The retained Gaussian inverse evaluation sums separately rounded powers. Its stated absolute-error interface permits quadratic accumulation even when the exact operator is positive and the approximation is odd and zero-preserving. An all-length exact family establishes that boundary; it does not contradict the existing `3p²/4` allowance or claim a defect in actual Gaussian rounding.

A fixed-source Horner replacement keeps every intermediate in the disk grid and has error `<p·2^-p`, using exactly the same `k−1` complete E calls. The written proof assumes `p>100`, `||E||≤0.42`, oracle error `<(p/3)2^-p`, and `||E^k||≤2^-p`. It includes initialization, exact subtraction, residual error, all stream scans and the complete wrapper cost. A separate counterexample shows why merely `||E||<1/2` does not suffice for the disk invariant.

At p=128 and k=64, the same valid contract fixture gives power-sum error `10528/3` grid units and Horner error `166/3`, with 63 calls each. The old error remains within the old allowance.

Only `research/neumann-rounding-audit/` is added (eight files). The alternative is implemented at its abstract oracle boundary. Actual Gaussian execution, analytic estimates, PR371's separate block-rounding repair, and physical integration remain open or inherited. No selected supplier, source, precision charge or exponent changes. No benchmark or new mathematical-method priority is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Research base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; seed **68**, adversarial-audit track; card `uniform-transfer-audit`, scope **refined** to this rounded precision implication.
- Submission main checked at `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983`: all three consumed source files and selected κ are unchanged. The complete patch applies to that main in a temporary Git index.
- Exact Git-blob/SHA256 source pins, three candidate tasks, bounded domains, stop rule and next questions are in SOURCES/TASK/VALIDATION. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1409.
- Fresh complete overlap snapshot: 791 open PRs and 148 discussion records. PR684 audits domain/windows, PR902 improves exact-power decay, and PR1243 audits inner packing. This adds rounded-error placement and a source-compatible abstract evaluator. None of those pending implementations is imported. Search coverage is not a novelty proof.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/neumann-rounding-audit
```

Expected: `PASS_NEUMANN_ROUNDING_AUDIT fixtures=648 family=326 controls=6`, ten passing tests, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`.

On macOS arm64 / CPython 3.12.13:

- 648 fixed matrix/oracle cases, all 35,640 states compared between integer and separate Fraction/block-matrix implementations; dense exact elimination supplies the final inverse oracle.
- 326 complete adverse-family cases through p=1024; six semantic controls cover wrong sign, missing half, omitted tail premise, overwritten source, weakened contraction margin and an unsupported linear bound for the old evaluator.
- Ten focused tests pass, including source/receipt corruption rejection, input/domain rejection, occupied-output preservation and optimized read-only relocation without Git.
- Optimized CPython 3.14.6 produces the identical canonical receipt. Selected-record integrity and all five existing selected-result tests pass. Metadata/source pins and whitespace checks pass.

Finite replay is separate from the written universal arguments. No selected cold replay, physical tape compiler execution, full historical suite, hosted-CI success, Lean theorem or independent human review is asserted.

Credit eumemic's PR5, icekylinx's retained interfaces, and the Harvey–van der Hoeven resampling lineage; Artus Krohn-Grimberghe's PR371, Effy Elden's PR684, Alan Grillo's PR902 and Hanson's PR1243 are distinct predecessor/context audits with exact heads recorded in the package. Ordinary Horner evaluation and contraction error analysis are standard methods.

Prepared by Hanson Sun (@bbMisk), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation, verification and writing. Apache-2.0; existing sources and notices are preserved.

## Open next questions

The README and TASK metadata specify two bounded follow-ups: connect the evaluator to an implemented, corrected Gaussian E routine; or derive a stronger actual-rounding property that excludes the adverse family for the original evaluator. The missing integrated routine/analytic adoption and missing stronger error law are explicit blockers. This PR does not perform either integration.
